# Audio Lore Chapter 10 — Kirivis: The Hero No One Knew

**Narrative script for TTS generation.**

---

Kirivis, the Demon King. In the history books, he is a monster — a warmonger who attacked the prosperous dragon empire of Baoth without warning, without cause, without honor. He killed hundreds of thousands. He destroyed the greatest civilization Erisdar had ever known. He was beheaded as a villain and the crowd cheered.

None of this is false. None of this is true, either.

The Glowing Tablet came to Kirivis when he was twenty-three years old. A Hybrian artifact, buried beneath the Demon Continent for millennia, activated by the blood of a wounded warrior who fell on the wrong patch of ground. It did not speak to him. It showed him. Fragments. Images. The truth in pieces, delivered one shard at a time over sixty years.

He saw the campfire on Old Earth, six thousand years before the Common Era. He saw the pre-philosophers who became the first Hybrian Shadows. He saw them seize power in 2030. He saw humanity enslaved and taken to the stars. He saw the rebel coalition form in the asteroid belt. He saw the refugee ships launched into the void. He saw three million years of war consuming galaxy after galaxy. He saw the Final Push, the mothership crashing into Old Earth, the Shadow empire shattered. He saw the Glorious Alliance crash into Ge'or's moon. He saw the Shadows survive — hibernating beneath Pontus, waiting, watching, manipulating every civilization that rose on this planet for over three thousand years.

And he saw what they were doing to Baoth.

The Shadows had infiltrated Goldenborn's court. Councilor Varik. Marshal Korr. High Scribe Elara. They whispered in the dragon emperor's ear. They possessed him — subtly at first, then completely. They turned Baoth's bureaucracy into a surveillance machine. They impoverished the population. They crushed dissent. And Goldenborn, isolated in his palace, believed the lies they fed him: the empire is thriving, the poverty is temporary, the people love you.

And Kirivis saw the endgame. The Shadows were engineering a sacrifice ceremony of unprecedented scale. The war itself would be the ritual. Every death would feed them. Every battle would advance their plan. When it was complete, the Shadows would have enough power to restart the Last Great War — and this time, there would be no coalition to stop them.

Kirivis spent a decade planning. He pretended to be insane so no one would take his ravings seriously. He built his army in secret. He prepared.

And then he attacked.

No explanation. No declaration of war. No chance for the Shadows to prepare. The Demonic War lasted forty-five years. Baoth, already weakened by internal decay, could not withstand the assault. The surveillance state, for all its sophistication, had neglected its military. Its legions were designed for internal control, not external defense.

In 421 BGD, Kirivis stormed the dragon hall. He stood before Goldenborn and told him the truth: the Shadows had used him. The war was the sacrifice ceremony. Every death had fed them. They had what they needed. Goldenborn was no longer necessary.

Rulfred — a Shadow in human form, celebrated throughout Baoth as a hero — revealed himself in that moment. He beheaded Kirivis before the assembled court. The crowd cheered. The Demon King was dead. The monster was slain.

They did not know he had just saved the world.

Kirivis took the truth to his grave. He died a villain in the eyes of history. But the Hybrian ritual was disrupted. The Shadows' plan was delayed by centuries. The sacrifice ceremony was incomplete. And Kirivis's adopted daughter, Nethra, would finish what he started — destroying Baoth entirely with the Gift from Three Million Years, creating the Leviathan Sea, and founding the Ironcloak.

The Demon King was the greatest hero Ge'or has ever known. No one remembers his name the way he deserved.

This chapter is for him.
